question: A vibrating guitar string produces very little sound on its own, until it is coupled to a soundboard. What is the physical reason a bare string is such a poor radiator of sound?

answers.text: An impedance mismatch between the string and the surrounding air reflects almost all the vibrational energy back into the string instead of into the air.
The string vibrates too slowly to disturb the air at all.
The string has no stiffness, so it cannot push on the air.
Sound cannot travel through a solid string.
